title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
abstract: arXiv:2611.28919v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual world models enable goal-conditioned planning by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions in latent space. However, planning depends on how well a model ranks candidates, whereas training optimizes how accurately it predicts each one. We identify the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the part of the cost error that can reorder candidates, and show that the more training reduces the DRR, the more it improves selection (Spearman $\rho = 0.82$, vs. $0.61$ for prediction error). Building on this insight, we introduce Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in selection rule that scores candidates by the standardized consensus of several independently trained checkpoints, which averages out their checkpoint-specific residuals. Across two model families (LeWorldModel and DINO-WM) and five tasks, DAS selects better actions than single checkpoints in 12 of 18 configurations and outperforms training one model three times longer in 14

translated_title: 何时更好的视觉世界模型才能制定更好的规划？面向潜在规划的决策对齐选择
translated_abstract: 视觉世界模型通过在潜在空间中预测候选动作的结果，来实现目标条件规划。然而，规划取决于模型对候选动作的排序好坏，而训练优化的却是模型对每个候选动作的预测精度。我们识别出决策相关残差（DRR），即代价误差中可能改变候选排序的部分，并证明训练对DRR的降低越多，对选择能力的提升越大（Spearman ρ = 0.82，而预测误差仅为0.61）。基于这一洞察，我们提出了决策对齐选择（DAS），这是一种即插即用的选择规则，通过多个独立训练检查点的标准化共识对候选动作打分，从而平均掉各检查点特有的残差。在两个模型家族（LeWorldModel和DINO-WM）和五项任务上，DAS在18个配置中的12个里选择了优于单一检查点的动作，并在14个配置中优于将单个模型训练三倍时长的效果。
tldr: 该论文揭示预测误差并不能决定规划质量，提出以决策相关残差（DRR）为理论依据的决策对齐选择（DAS）规则，通过多个独立训练检查点的标准化共识为候选动作打分，从而在潜在规划中显著提升动作选择效果。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that prediction error does not determine planning quality and introduces Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in rule that scores candidate actions by the standardized consensus of multiple independently trained checkpoints, yielding better plans in latent planning.
